text:
The evidence can't say whether storm damage caused the loss. It confirms that tree-cover loss happened but says nothing about why.

What it does show:
- About 4.5 ha of tree-cover loss was mapped in 2023, roughly 0.12% of the 3,643.5 ha asset.
- The area was forest in 2020, and later years of the series were observed, so the loss is corroborated.
- Most of the affected area (4.3 ha) is mapped as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda).

The tool states explicitly that it does not establish cause. Harvest, fire, storm and clearing all look the same in this data. Cutting a plantation also counts as tree-cover loss. The forest map gives context only, never cause.

Storm damage is therefore neither confirmed nor ruled out. To test it, you would need other evidence, such as weather event records for 2023, the operator's harvest or management records, or a field or high-resolution imagery review of the patch.
